# Artifact Keeper 1.11.14

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 23 changelog entries from 18 pull requests since 1.11.13, all landed on `main` first and brought to the line in #5740, #5746, #5747, #5781, #5842, #5843, #5850, #5851, #5852, #5853, #5854, #5861, #5878, #5916, #5938, #5997, #6036 and #6038. Most of it is sign-in hardening: **a federated account is bound to the identity provider that created it** (#5483), **a password alone no longer gets past TOTP or the SSO-only login policy** (#5484), **CI token exchange and OIDC sign-in require `iss` and `aud`** (#5482), **every password check has a login budget** (#5485), and **Basic and OCI credentials carrying an API token are checked as tokens first**, so a dead token no longer runs a bcrypt or trips the auth-capacity `503` (#5640, #5683). **Quotas change shape**: repository and project quota refusals answer `403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` instead of `507` and are checked before the body is read, and **instance-wide storage and monthly transfer quotas** are new and off by default (#5912). **A storage outage answers `503` within seconds instead of hanging**, and full storage answers `507` (#5649, #5650). Credential settings can be read from **`<NAME>_FILE` secret mounts** (#4142). **Two schema migrations**: 350 binds federated accounts to their provider and 380 adds the shared transfer-quota counter; the line moves from migration 339 to 380. **Read the upgrade notes before upgrading** if you configure more than one OIDC, SAML or LDAP provider of the same type, send passwords for TOTP-enrolled accounts from automation, treat `507` as "over quota", verify the legacy `X-Webhook-Signature` header, or run behind an environment HTTP proxy.

## Upgrade notes

- **If you configure more than one OIDC, SAML or LDAP provider of the same type, check your federated accounts before upgrading** (#5483, migration 350). A federated account is now bound to the provider that created it. Migration 350 binds an existing account only where its provider is certain: an LDAP account to the provider it last signed in through, and every account of a type with exactly one configured provider to that provider. Any other existing federated account is refused at sign-in with `403 FORBIDDEN` and a `LOGIN_FAILED` audit event whose `details.reason` is `federated_account_unlinked`, until an administrator binds it (`UPDATE users SET auth_provider_id = '<provider id>' WHERE id = '<user id>';`). No second account is created beside it. CI service accounts are unchanged. See `docs/sso-account-binding.md`.
- **A user who signs in through two providers of the same type now needs one account per provider** (#5483). Before 1.11.14, two LDAP providers on one directory (a primary and a replica, or one with a CA certificate and one without) found the same account for a DN. Now an account belongs to one provider: the provider that created it, or for an LDAP account from before the upgrade, the provider it last signed in through. A sign-in through the other provider tries to create a second account, and gets `409 Conflict` when the username or email is taken. **Keep one provider per directory, or have users sign in through the provider their account is bound to** (`users.auth_provider_id`; see `docs/sso-account-binding.md`). Letting an administrator link providers that share a directory is tracked in #6034.
- **Automation that sends the password of a TOTP-enrolled account must switch to an API token** (#5484). HTTP Basic `username:password` on `/api/v1` now gets the same `401` as a wrong password for an account with TOTP enrolled, an account the TOTP enforcement policy requires to enrol, or a non-admin local account while an SSO provider is enabled, as `POST /api/v1/auth/login` already refused them (the verified-admin break-glass is kept). On the format and registry routes, a password for an account with TOTP enrolled gets `401`, as `/v2/token` already answered. Use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or the token as the Basic password on format routes. LDAP login and the OIDC and SAML exchange codes now return the `/auth/login` TOTP challenge (`totp_required: true`, a `totp_token` to redeem at `POST /api/v1/auth/totp/verify`) for an enrolled user; a web UI that does not show a TOTP step after LDAP or SSO sign-in cannot complete those sign-ins. See `docs/two-factor-and-passwords.md`.
- **An upload over a repository or project quota answers `403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, not `507`** (#5912). The `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` code is unchanged; the JSON body adds `scope`, `repository`, `project`, `limit_bytes` and `used_bytes`, and the chunked upload API's session-create check answers the same `403` instead of `413`. The refusal is checked on `Content-Length` before the body is read. A backend whose storage is actually full still answers `507 STORAGE_FULL`. **If a script or CI job treats `507` as "over quota", match `403` with the `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` code as well.** Peer replication treats the new `403` as an item rejection.
- **A caller who cannot write a repository gets the permission refusal, never quota figures** (#5912, in #6038). The quota pre-check answers a quota refusal only to a caller who passes the repository's write gate; anyone else gets `401` (anonymous) or `403 FORBIDDEN` (`DENIED` on `/v2`), as before the pre-check existed.
- **`MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` is checked before the body is read** (#5912). An upload whose declared `Content-Length` is over the limit is refused at once with a JSON `413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` carrying `limit_bytes` (and `content_length`), or the OCI envelope's `SIZE_INVALID` on `/v2`, and the connection is closed; a body without a length is cut off with the same `413` once it crosses the limit. This includes Git LFS object uploads, which now get the JSON `413` before any bytes are streamed. If a reverse proxy in front of the backend enforces its own body limit, set it above `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE` so the backend's JSON `413` is the answer clients see.
- **The legacy `X-Webhook-Signature` header changes value** (#5234). It is now `sha256=HMAC(secret, body)`, the documented form. A receiver that recomputed it over `"<t>.<body>"` stops verifying after the upgrade: switch it to the `v1=` token in `X-ArtifactKeeper-Signature` (same inputs, with replay protection) or to an HMAC over the body alone. `X-ArtifactKeeper-Signature` is unchanged.
- **Destinations sent through an environment proxy are now checked against the outbound address policy** (#5459). With `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` or `ALL_PROXY` set (any case), a destination the backend resolves to a private address is refused unless `UPSTREAM_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` or `AK_SSRF_ALLOW_PRIVATE_CIDRS` admits it, as on the direct path. This affects internal mirrors and private storage endpoints reached through a corporate proxy. The backend now resolves proxied host names itself and refuses one it cannot resolve; where it can reach DNS only through the proxy, give it a resolver or set `AK_UPSTREAM_ENV_PROXY=ignore`.
- **A Basic password shaped exactly like an API token or an Artifact Keeper JWT is only tried as that token** (#5640, #5683). A local password of that exact shape no longer works as a Basic password on any route; it still works at `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.
- **Failed Basic password checks are budgeted** (#5485). Failed verifications are counted per (username, source IP) in a bucket sized like `RATE_LIMIT_TOKEN_EXCHANGE_PER_WINDOW`; past it that pair answers `429` with `Retry-After` before any bcrypt. Correct passwords are never counted. LDAP login now shares the login endpoint's limiters. A client that retries a wrong password in a loop sees `429` sooner.
- **Migrations.** 350 adds `users.auth_provider_id` and backfills it where the provider is certain; adding the nullable column takes a brief `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on `users`, which first waits for open transactions on the table, and the backfill rewrites the matched federated rows once. 380 adds the shared `transfer_quota_usage` counter. Both are the same files as on `main`, so the migration ledger stays consistent with 1.12.

New settings, all optional:

- **Quotas:** `STORAGE_QUOTA_BYTES` and `TRANSFER_QUOTA_BYTES` (both off by default), `STORAGE_QUOTA_WARN_PERCENT` and `TRANSFER_QUOTA_WARN_PERCENT` (default 80), `TRANSFER_QUOTA_GRACE_PERCENT` (default 0) and `QUOTA_HELP_URL` (#5912). See `docs/operations/instance-quotas.md`.
- **Storage timeouts:** `STORAGE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 3), `STORAGE_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 15) and `STORAGE_BULK_RETRY_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 180) (#5649).
- **Secret files:** a `_FILE` companion for every credential-typed setting (#4142); see `docs/operations/file-based-secrets.md`.
- `AK_UPSTREAM_ENV_PROXY=ignore` keeps upstream fetches off the environment proxy (#5459).

## Security

- **Federated accounts are bound to their identity provider** (#5483, in #5843). With two OIDC, SAML or LDAP providers configured, a user of one provider whose `sub`, NameID or DN equalled a user of the other was signed in as that user, inheriting its `is_admin` and tokens. Sign-in now matches on the provider too; see the upgrade notes.
- **A password alone no longer gets past TOTP or the SSO-only login policy** (#5484, in #5861). Basic auth on `/api/v1`, on the format routes and on OCI, LDAP login, the OIDC callback and the SAML ACS skipped the second-factor and SSO-only checks that `POST /api/v1/auth/login` applies, so a TOTP-enrolled user's password alone could mint a non-expiring API token.
- **CI token exchange and OIDC sign-in require `iss` and `aud`; a disabled SSO provider no longer signs anyone in; a blank OIDC `sub` is refused** (#5482, in #5842). A validly signed assertion without `aud` was exchanged for any provider on its issuer, a disabled provider was only hidden from the list, and every token with an empty `sub` signed in as one shared account.
- **Every password check has a login budget, and a cancelled request no longer frees its bcrypt slot early** (#5485, in #5861). The auth-concurrency permit is held by the bcrypt job itself; LDAP login and Basic passwords on every surface are rate-limited; an unknown username runs the same bcrypt as a real one on Basic and `/v2/token`; the SSO HTTP client has connect and request timeouts.
- **Environment-proxy destinations are checked against the outbound address policy** (#5459, in #5781). Under an uppercase or lowercase proxy variable a Remote's host name went to the proxy without checking where it resolved, so with private upstreams disabled a repository administrator could have a sync fetch loopback content.
- **The virtual member listing no longer reveals private repositories** (#5612, in #5853). A caller who cannot read the repository now gets the same `404` as for an unknown key, instead of a `400` or `403` that told an existing private virtual apart.
- **A curation or npm scope-policy pattern with many `*` wildcards can no longer stall requests** (#5716, in #5854). The glob matcher was exponential in the number of wildcards; it is now linear in pattern length times name length, matching the same names.
- **quinn-udp moves to 0.5.16 for RUSTSEC-2026-0538** (#5935, in #5938). The crate is only reachable through `reqwest`'s HTTP/3 support, which the backend does not build, so this clears the audit finding rather than a runtime exposure.
- **The backend and OpenSCAP images carry a time-boxed exception for 14 `krb5-libs` CVEs** (#5995, in #5997). Trivy reports CVE-2026-107364 and 13 siblings (all HIGH) against `krb5-libs-1.21.1-10.el9_8.1`; the fixed build is in the entitled RHEL 9 repositories but not yet in UBI 9, so neither image can install it. `krb5-libs` is present only as a library dependency of `libcurl`; neither image ships a KDC or `kadmind`, every one of the 14 is a KDC or `kadmind` server bug, and nothing uses Kerberos. The IDs are in `.trivyignore` with an expiry of 2026-12-14, and the rootfs upgrade picks up the fixed build as soon as UBI ships it. This is what lets Docker Publish publish the line again.
- **The manual `publish-binaries.yml` workflow is retired** (#5960, in #6036). A dispatch with a free-text tag could replace a published release's binaries with an unsigned rebuild from another ref. `release.yml` is the only release path; nothing that ships changes.

## What changed

- **Quotas** (#5912, in #5916 and #6038). New instance-wide `STORAGE_QUOTA_BYTES` refuses every write that would store new bytes with `403 STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (downloads, deletes, listing, sign-in and settings are never refused; a remote repository keeps serving but stops caching). New `TRANSFER_QUOTA_BYTES` caps artifact download bytes per UTC calendar month, counted across replicas; at the hard limit artifact downloads answer `429 TRANSFER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` with `Retry-After` until the next month, while metadata, uploads and the API keep working. Refusals use the OCI envelope on `/v2` (`DENIED`, `TOOMANYREQUESTS`, `SIZE_INVALID`) and npm's `error` field on npm routes. `GET /api/v1/system/quota` and `GET /api/v1/admin/stats` report the quotas, with new `ak_storage_*`, `ak_transfer_*` and `ak_quota_refusals_total{kind}` metrics.
- **Storage outages and full storage** (#5649, #5650, in #5740). With the object store unreachable, uploads and downloads answer `503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` with `Retry-After` (OCI: `503 UNAVAILABLE`) within about 15 to 30 seconds instead of hanging for minutes. A write refused for lack of space answers `507 STORAGE_FULL` (OCI: `507 INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE`) instead of `500`, and no object-store error text (bucket names, request ids) reaches a client. `/health` and `/readyz` are unchanged on this line.
- **API tokens over Basic** (#5640, #5633, in #5746; #5683, in #5861). A Basic password or Bearer `base64(user:secret)` shaped like an API token or JWT is resolved only as that token: no bcrypt, no failed-login write, no auth-capacity permit. Basic with a token is no longer about 30 times slower than Bearer, so `pixi install` through a conda Virtual no longer aborts on `503 Authentication service is at capacity`, and an expired, revoked or unknown token answers `401`, not `503`.
- **Secret files** (#4142, in #5878; #4819, in #5878). Every credential-typed setting accepts a `<NAME>_FILE` companion naming a mounted secret; the direct value wins when both are set, and an unreadable or empty file is an error naming the variable and path. `DATABASE_URL_FILE` now takes effect in the published image despite its baked placeholder.
- **Repository-scoped storage keys for 18 more formats on cloud storage** (#5662, in #5851). Go, Swift, Pub, Ansible, Chef, CocoaPods, CRAN, Puppet, Protobuf, Composer, JetBrains, Helm, Hugging Face, Bazel, Terraform, RubyGems, VS Code and Hex wrote hosted packages to flat keys on S3, GCS and Azure, so a second repository publishing the same version failed with `409 CONFLICT`. New objects go under the repository id; existing objects keep serving, nothing is migrated, and filesystem storage and `STORAGE_KEY_SCHEME=flat` are unchanged. Hugging Face file paths are now limited to 1999 characters.
- **Replication** (#5625, in #5850). Adding, changing or removing an artifact label no longer sends a delete to peers subscribed to its repository by hand.
- **Webhooks** (#5234, in #5747). The legacy `X-Webhook-Signature` now signs the body alone, as documented; see the upgrade notes.
- **Protobuf** (#5197, in #5747). A `Download` naming no commit or label returns the latest commit for a module with one commit, instead of a `500`.
- **Scanning** (#5830, in #5852). A manual scan that stops before its scanners run (unreadable bytes, a deleted artifact, a database error) marks its unfinished rows `failed` with the reason at once, instead of leaving them `running` for 30 minutes until the janitor.
- **Proxy quarantine release** (#6043, in #6064). After an admin releases a held proxied path while its background fetch is still running, every download that follows is served, instead of an intermittent `409 "Artifact is quarantined and pending security review"`.
- **Permission lookups during a database outage** (#6052, in #6054). A format-route read (a Git LFS batch, npm metadata) whose permission check cannot reach the database answers `503` with `Retry-After: 1`, as writes already did, so clients back off and retry.
- **Release pipeline** (#6105, #6106, #6118, #6107, #6129, #6140). `release.yml` ends green when the release was published, a candidate can rerun only its failed gate groups once, and a merge can no longer cancel a candidate's image build. Nothing that ships changes.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.14]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.14/CHANGELOG.md).
